entries.name: Retirement administration
entries.definition: Running retirement plans for employers or members, including enrolment, contributions, benefit calculations and record-keeping.

entries.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
entries.definition: Grounding generated output with retrieved information.

entries.name: Return-to-work management
entries.definition: Helping injured or ill employees get back to work through planned, modified or gradual duties, usually alongside insurers and health providers.

entries.name: Revising legal documents
entries.definition: Editing legal documents such as contracts and agreements to correct errors and update their terms.

entries.name: Rhinoceros 3D
entries.definition: Computer-aided design software from Robert McNeel & Associates for modelling free-form 3D curves and surfaces, widely used in architecture and product design.

entries.name: Ribosomal intergenic spacer analysis
entries.definition: A DNA fingerprinting technique that compares the length of the spacer between two ribosomal RNA genes to profile the bacteria in a sample.

entries.name: Rigging (computer animation)
entries.definition: Building the skeleton, joints and controls that let a 3D model be posed and animated.

entries.name: Right to Financial Privacy Act
entries.definition: A 1978 US federal law that limits when government agencies may obtain a person's records from financial institutions.

entries.name: RightNow CRM
entries.definition: A cloud customer service and customer relationship management product from RightNow Technologies, which Oracle bought in 2011.

entries.name: Rights issue
entries.definition: An offer that lets existing shareholders buy new shares in proportion to their holding, usually at a discount, so that the company can raise capital.

entries.name: Riot.js
entries.definition: A small client-side JavaScript library for building user interfaces from custom elements.

entries.name: RISA-3D
entries.definition: Structural analysis and design software from RISA Technologies for modelling buildings, bridges and other structures in three dimensions.

entries.name: Risk adjustment coding
entries.definition: Assigning diagnosis codes from medical records so that health plans can be paid according to how sick their members are.

entries.name: Risk aggregation
entries.definition: Combining risk measures from different business lines, risk types or positions into one view of an organisation's total risk.

entries.name: Risk awareness
entries.definition: Recognising hazards and potential harm and understanding how likely and how serious they are.

entries.name: Risk exposure assessment
entries.definition: Working out how far a person, organisation or asset is exposed to a risk and how large the possible loss or harm is.

entries.name: Risk management
entries.definition: Identifying, assessing and controlling threats to an organisation's capital, earnings or operations.

entries.name: Risk management planning
entries.definition: Deciding how risks on a project or in an organisation will be identified, assessed, handled and monitored, and recording that in a plan.

entries.name: Risk ratings
entries.definition: Scores or grades that show how likely and how serious a risk is, as in credit risk ratings and risk matrices.

entries.name: Robomongo
entries.definition: A free graphical client for browsing and querying MongoDB databases, later renamed Robo 3T.

entries.name: Rockmelt
entries.definition: A social web browser, based on Chromium, that was discontinued after Yahoo bought its maker in 2013.

entries.name: Rockwell FactoryTalk
entries.definition: Rockwell Automation's family of industrial software for operator screens, data historians, production management and analytics.

entries.name: Role-based access control
entries.definition: An approach to restricting system access in which permissions are assigned to roles and users receive access through the roles they hold.

entries.name: Rolling stock
entries.definition: The vehicles that run on a railway, such as locomotives, passenger carriages and freight wagons, and the engineering that goes with them.

entries.name: Roof bolting
entries.definition: Installing steel bolts into the roof of an underground mine or tunnel to hold the rock together and prevent roof falls.

entries.name: Route management
entries.definition: Planning and supervising the routes that vehicles follow, including schedules, stops and drivers, so that deliveries or services run efficiently.

entries.name: Routing Table Maintenance Protocol
entries.definition: A routing protocol of the AppleTalk network suite that lets routers share which networks they can reach.

entries.name: RSA Archer
entries.definition: A governance, risk and compliance platform for managing risks, policies, audits and compliance work in one place.

entries.name: Rubber-tyred metro
entries.definition: A metro system whose trains run on rubber tyres on concrete or steel guideways instead of steel wheels on steel rails.

entries.name: Rx30
entries.definition: A pharmacy management software product used to process prescriptions and run pharmacy operations.

entries.name: RxKotlin
entries.definition: A Kotlin library that adds language-friendly extensions on top of RxJava for writing reactive, event-driven programs.

entries.name: Safe Drinking Water Act
entries.definition: The US federal law that sets standards for the quality of public drinking water and requires water systems to meet them.

entries.name: Safety audits
entries.definition: Checking workplaces, equipment and procedures against safety rules to find hazards and non-compliance.

entries.name: Sage Intacct
entries.definition: Cloud-based accounting and financial management software, originally from Intacct Corporation and now owned by Sage.

entries.name: Sage MAS 90
entries.definition: Accounting and business management software from Sage for small and mid-sized companies, later sold as Sage 100.

entries.name: Sailing instruction
entries.definition: Teaching people how to sail.

entries.name: SailPoint IdentityIQ
entries.definition: SailPoint's identity governance software for managing user access, access reviews and account provisioning across an organisation's systems.

entries.name: Sails.js
entries.definition: A Node.js web framework, modelled on the MVC pattern, for building data-driven APIs and apps.

entries.name: Sales and operations planning
entries.definition: A regular business process in which sales, operations and finance teams agree one plan that balances demand forecasts with supply and capacity.

entries.name: Sales journal
entries.definition: An accounting journal in which a business records the sales it makes on credit.
